policy: all resolutions publish, including misses and downgrades

entries.story_title: Diplomacy over reopening the Strait of Hormuz
entries.claim_text: Japan's Kyodo News reported that Iran offered to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within seven days if the United States takes steps toward easing military pressure.
entries.reason: A senior Iranian official independently described to Reuters the conditional Hormuz-reopening proposal (conveyed via mediators September 16, delegation with full authority), corroborating the September 22 Kyodo report carried by the Wall Street Journal.

entries.question: After Tuesday's expected Trump-GCC meeting, does Trump clarify his 'big decision' on Iran — and is the Axios 'annihilate' quote confirmed by a vetted outlet?
entries.resolution_text: Yes on both parts: at the UNGA podium on September 22 Trump clarified the 'big decision' as make-a-deal or 'annihilate the Islamic Republic... quickly,' plus 'total economic isolation of Iran' and a predicted post-midterms deal — and the AP reported the speech, giving the 'annihilate' language vetted-outlet confirmation.

entries.story_title: Ship attacks in the Strait of Hormuz
entries.claim_text: UKMTO reported Monday that a tanker sailing into the Strait of Hormuz was struck by an unknown projectile, leaving two crew members with minor injuries.
entries.reason: Reuters on September 22 identified the struck vessel as the Isle of Man-flagged crude tanker LR Stephanie, managed by Universal Tanker Corp., and confirmed two crew injuries — corroborating the September 21 UKMTO report of a tanker hit by an unknown projectile while entering the strait.

entries.question: Does oil's 'diplomatic discount' hold through UNGA week, or does another Houthi strike on Saudi infrastructure erase it and push Brent back toward $110?
entries.resolution_text: The discount deepened rather than eroding: Brent fell to $97.76 on September 22 after Iran's conditional Hormuz-reopening offer, and no Houthi strike on Saudi infrastructure was reported to erase it; $110 remains distant.

entries.story_title: Houthi west-coast offensive / govt counter-offensive around Mokha
entries.claim_text: US officials told CNN the United States has no plans for a counteroffensive against the Houthis despite their push toward Bab el-Mandeb; Washington's strategy is to rely on Saudi Arabia, though there are real doubts inside the US government that the Saudis can stop the Houthis al
entries.reason: The New York Times' September 21 reporting that Trump called off prepared Sunday strikes on the Houthis, plus Reuters' report that he made no pledge of military help to al-Alimi, independently corroborate CNN's September 19 US-officials reporting that Washington has no plans for a counteroffensive and is relying on Saudi Arabia.

entries.story_title: Houthi west-coast offensive / govt counter-offensive around Mokha
entries.claim_text: CBS News reported, citing two sources, that Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman personally asked President Trump to take military action against the Houthis; the report has not been confirmed by a vetted outlet.
entries.reason: The New York Times (via Reuters) reports the administration prepared strikes Sunday after fresh pleas from Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, independently corroborating CBS's September 19 reporting that MBS personally asked Trump to take military action against the Houthis.

entries.story_title: Houthi west-coast offensive / govt counter-offensive around Mokha
entries.claim_text: WSJ (three officials): the Houthi strike apparently hit jet-fuel facilities at King Khalid International Airport; an AFP journalist on the ground saw firefighters tackling a burning Aramco-branded fuel tank at a depot near the airport; this is the first direct assault on Riyadh i
entries.reason: The September 20 Reuters video of a massive black-smoke plume near Riyadh's main international airport, plus Saudi Arabia's confirmation of a dawn ballistic-missile intercept, corroborate the WSJ's September 19 reporting (via three officials plus an AFP ground journalist) that a Houthi strike set a jet-fuel depot ablaze at the airport.

entries.story_title: U.S. embassy security alerts across the Middle East
entries.question: Do more U.S. missions post September 19-style alerts tomorrow, and does the language escalate from vigilance to something harder?
entries.resolution_text: Yes — more missions posted alerts on September 19-20: the U.S. Embassy in Israel, the U.S. virtual embassy in Iran, and a State Department Middle East alert, plus a concrete step (personnel travel restricted to Taif and Yanbu without authorization). Language stayed at vigilance and flight-disruption, not harder.

entries.story_title: Houthi west-coast offensive / govt counter-offensive around Mokha
entries.question: Does Riyadh name a cause for the two Saturday-morning explosions over the capital — a Houthi drone, an interception, or something else?
entries.resolution_text: The 3 AM Riyadh alert/explosions are now a confirmed Houthi missile/drone strike on jet-fuel facilities at King Khalid International Airport (WSJ, three officials).

entries.question: Does the Fed raise rates by 25bp at the 2pm ET decision, and how do markets react with Brent above $107 and the 10-year above 5%?
entries.resolution_text: The FOMC voted unanimously 12-0 to raise the benchmark rate a quarter point to 3.75%-4.00%, the first hike since 2023, under new Chair Kevin Warsh. Markets reacted sharply: the Dow fell 631 points, the 10-year Treasury yield closed just above 5% for the first time in 19 years, and Brent slid 2.7% to $105.83 on expected demand cooling.

entries.story_title: Ship attacks in the Strait of Hormuz
entries.claim_text: India's Ministry of External Affairs said the Panamanian-flagged MT El Gaia, carrying 14 Indians, was attacked off the Omani coast on Sunday; 13 have been rescued and search operations continue for one missing crew member.
entries.reason: The IMO now reports two seafarers missing from the El Gaia while India's foreign ministry reports one — the casualty figures directly conflict, so the rescue and missing counts in the Sept 13 claim are contested.

entries.story_title: Diplomacy over reopening the Strait of Hormuz
entries.claim_text: A senior Iranian official told Reuters no signed agreement is expected from Monday's Muscat meeting, saying Iran still wants to collect transit fees from ships using the strait, which Oman rejects.
entries.reason: The Monday Muscat meeting was postponed before it happened, so no signed agreement resulted — the outcome the senior Iranian official predicted on Sept 12; the evening edition explicitly noted Pezeshkian's signing claim was undercut by that official's account.

entries.story_title: Drone attack shuts Saudi East-West pipeline
entries.claim_text: Trump said Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman called him twice Thursday urging U.S. strikes on the Houthis as they advanced in Yemen; Trump declined, saying the U.S. is focused on freedom of navigation.
entries.reason: CNN, citing a source familiar with the calls, confirmed that MBS phoned Trump twice last week seeking US strikes on the Houthis and that Trump declined to intervene — matching Trump's own Sept 12 account of the calls.

entries.claim_text: Brent settled Friday at $104.61/bbl (down 2.8% on the day, up 8.7% on the week); WTI fell to $100.05 (up 9.4% on the week), with the pullback aided by reports of Oman's planned Hormuz meeting.
entries.reason: WSJ independently confirmed Friday's $104.61 Brent settle and the 8.7% weekly gain, matching the figure from the Sept 12 edition — two independent reputable outlets now agree.

entries.question: Does the Saudi Sohar STS workaround keep Brent from retesting $110?
entries.resolution_text: No — as of September 21 Brent fell for a fourth straight session to $101.94 on improved Hormuz flows and UNGA diplomacy hopes, staying well below $110; the Sohar STS workaround plus the diplomacy window kept prices from retesting the high.
